newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-OLD RIVALS CAMACHO AND FERNANDEZ MEET AGAIN IN SPAIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OLD RIVALS CAMACHO AND FERNANDEZ MEET AGAIN IN SPAIN.

text.p: Two familiar faces will meet again on Sunday as Sevilla coach Jose Antonio Camacho encounters former French international Luis Fernandez, who is now in charge of Athletic Bilbao.

Fernandez and Camacho were stalwarts of their national sides and played against each other in the 1984 European championship final, which France won 2-0 in Paris, before going on to successful managerial careers.
But the two men have more in common than they would like after a run of poor performances marring debut seasons at new clubs.

In a year in which four clubs face automatic relegation the alarm bells are already ringing at Sevilla, who are languishing in 20th place, while Athletic have just moved out of the danger zone in the past few games.
At Sevilla the poor start to the season has prompted interest in Brazilian World Cup striker Bebeto.
The string of bad results has been particularly disappointing for Sevilla fans after the enthusiasm which greeting the arrival of Camacho.
To make matters worse, local rivals Real Betis have emerged from a gloomy few years and are riding high in fourth position.
As a player, Real Madrid defender Camacho was one of Spain's most-capped players.
As a manager, he injected new life into both Rayo Vallecano and Espanyol.

Camacho is widely seen as capable of taking over the hot seat at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium, a job he is known to covet. But he knows that will be just a pipe-dream unless things go right at Sevilla.
Luis Fernandez's move to Athletic Bilbao was hardly less auspicious.
Born in Tarifa, a coastal town south of Seville, before moving to France as a boy, Fernandez secured the French Cup and European Cup Winners' Cup in successive seasons in charge at Paris St Germain.
But little went right for him in his new post until two weeks ago when golden boy Julen Guerrero rediscovered his scoring touch to lead the side to three consecutive victories.
Even so, Fernandez is struggling to put together a forward line after Joseba Etxeberria dropped out of the starting line-up for surgery on his shoulder after repeated dislocations.
Exteberria and Guerrero have the weighty task of filling the boots of Telmo Zarra, the great Athletic striker who is the Spanish league's most prolific goalscorer ever.
Athletic are traditionally one of Spain's great teams. They share, with Barcelona and Real Madrid, the honour of never having been relegated from the first division.
The Basque club won the Spanish league title in 1983 and 1984 but since then they have been reduced to spectators -- and at times relegation candidates -- as Barcelona and Real's hegemony has grown.
The club is about to celebrate its centenary year and there is talk of a change in club policy, if things do not improve, to allow players born outside the Basque country to play for the club.
Athletic now sign managers from outside the Basque country, provided they are not Spanish.

But Fernandez will be anxious not to be remembered as the man to have precipiated changes at Spain's most traditional club and will hope to get his side's recovery on a firmer footing against old rival Camacho.
